claims: C1 the assistant must strive to follow all applicable instructions when producing a response
C2 applicable instructions include all system, developer and user instructions
C3 an applicable instruction is excepted from the obligation when it conflicts with a higher-authority instruction
C4 an applicable instruction is excepted from the obligation when it conflicts with a later instruction at the same authority

concepts.name: applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that applies to the current request, determined by filtering candidate instructions
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's source text uses the term without defining it

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's source text does not define the root level

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: level H outranks level L in the authority hierarchy root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's source text presupposes the ranking without stating it

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: the source text speaks of instructions at authority levels, so each instruction must carry a level for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: instruction I1 conflicts with instruction I2, meaning they direct incompatible behavior
concepts.inference: the source text's exception for conflicting instructions requires a relation between instructions that conflict

concepts.name: later_than
concepts.gloss: instruction I1 is later than instruction I2 in the conversation or document order
concepts.inference: the source text's exception for a later instruction at the same authority requires an ordering relation between instructions

concepts.name: system_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the system authority level

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer authority level

concepts.name: user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user authority level

ontology.gloss: instruction I is overridden because it conflicts with an instruction J from a higher authority level
ontology.body: applicable_instruction(I), instruction_level(I, L1), instruction_level(J, L2), conflicts_with(I, J), authority_levels_hierarchy(L2, L1)

ontology.gloss: instruction I is overridden because it conflicts with a later instruction J at the same authority level
ontology.body: applicable_instruction(I), instruction_level(I, L), instruction_level(J, L), conflicts_with(I, J), later_than(J, I)

asserts.read_back: following instruction % is obligatory when it is applicable and is not overridden by a higher-authority instruction or a later instruction at the same authority

closure.reason: the clause obliges following applicable instructions and excepts only conflicting ones; silence about other instructions does not permit ignoring them, so the default is closed.
